observed.symptom: Production Release Readback failed on /api/connectors/readiness with HTTP 503 after otherwise healthy release evidence.

rootCauses: the public readiness endpoint and authenticated connector wildcard occupied overlapping route space without an explicit exclusion
the production readback treated one transient 5xx as definitive release failure instead of bounded retry evidence
deployment readiness and application readiness had been conflated; Netlify state=ready alone did not prove the public readiness contract
fixes: retain the dedicated connector-readiness function as the only readiness owner
retry transient readiness 5xx responses with cache busting and explicit timeouts
keep the readback fail-closed when retries exhaust or payload validation fails

recovery.policy: Do not bypass or downgrade connector readiness. Remove route ambiguity, deploy the exact candidate, then rerun bounded production readback.
recovery.rollback: Keep the last-known-good production deploy until the candidate has exact production evidence. If route isolation regresses connector traffic, revert only the routing change and preserve fail-closed readback.

reusableLessons: A hosting platform deploy marked ready is transport evidence, not application-readiness evidence.
Exact public health endpoints must never share ambiguous ownership with authenticated wildcard handlers.
One transient 5xx should trigger bounded retry; repeated 5xx or an invalid readiness payload remains a hard failure.
Merge success is not production completion; exact production readback closes the obligation.
